course_name_original: French B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
course_name_en: French B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
prerequisites: The minimum language requirement is level A-2 in accordance with the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

learning_outcomes.text: Can clearly present conclusions and opinions related to general, academic and professional issues in a written and oral form.

Can understand extensive, even detailed texts and oral statements, for example, lectures and presentations, when they relate to the field of study and contemporary issues. Can interpret obtained data and information.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and professional topics. Can take an active part in discussions with a suitable degree of fluency and spontaneity, also in the professional environment.

Can write a clear, informative and argumentative text related to general issues, as well as the field of study. Can write letters and other types of correspondence typical of work environment. Can effectively use educational and learning materials.

Can use grammatical structures, phraseology and vocabulary necessary to understand general interest texts, contemporary socio-economic texts, academic texts and special interest texts related to the field of study, and ones that enable interaction with a degree of fluency and spontaneity for academic and professional purposes.

syllabus_topics: GRAMMAR - simple and compound relative pronouns - emphasis - comparison - adverbs - future tenses (futur simple, futur proche, futur antérieur) - past tenses (passé composé, imparfait, plus-que parfait) - indirect speech, concordance of tenses - agreement of the past participle with the subject or direct object - nominalization - present participle, gerund - conditional, hypothetical sentences - adverbial pronouns, personal pronouns, double pronouns - indefinite pronouns - passé simple

THEMES AND VOCABULARY - Description of a person (external appearance, character traits, personality, requirements related to specific professions). - Consumer society (online shopping, contemporary consumer attitudes, auction sites, sales phenomenon, fair trade, household budget, student budget). - Education (teaching and learning methods, French educational system, higher education in France, course formats, student life). - Elements of specialized and general technical language. - Work (CV, job interview, job market, job offers, employment conditions). Work organization in a company. - Media (press, radio, television) in France and Europe, reader/listener/viewer profile, the phenomenon of Francophonie). - Civil society (associations, humanitarian actions, social mobilization) - Citizenship (associations, humanitarian actions, social mobilization). - Culture and art (emblematic figures of French culture and art, painting, theatre, cinema). - Ecology (threats, environmental protection, sustainable development, renewable energies). - Tourism, travel, multiculturalism.

LANGUAGE AND LANGUAGE FUNCTIONS - giving advice - expressing feelings - congratulating, reproaching - writing a letter / email requesting information, clarification - conducting research on French websites - writing a letter / email with a complaint, a claim - negotiating the price, - preventing a danger - presenting professional qualifications - drafting a CV, a cover letter, a letter in the context of business correspondence - completing documents to undertake studies in France - completing documents to find employment in France - expressing consent - expressing opposition, prohibiting something - public speaking, - writing an informational text - writing a comment, a review - expressing cause and effect - doubting, relating unconfirmed events - expressing certainty and doubts - writing a petition, a letter of protest - expressing purpose - expressing duration - arguing and convincing - writing an internship report - talking about the future, making hypotheses - relating events, providing arguments - convincing, presenting arguments - planning a trip - understanding popular scientific articles - understanding texts in the field of one's specialization
assessment_rules: To receive an end-of-semester pass mark, all tests during the semester must be passed. If a student fails a test at the first attempt, they can resit it twice. A pass mark at the second attempt replaces the fail mark; a pass mark at the third attempt results in an average of the two marks (fail and pass), which must not be lower than 3.0. The final grade is calculated as the average of the exam grade and the end-of-semester grades obtained in all semesters before the final language exam. Unexcused absence in more than 7 classes may result in a fail mark for the semester, regardless of test results.
